My Palomar submission failed during the Palomar-owned trusted-cache stage:

https://github.com/PalomarRegistry/PalomarSubmission/actions/runs/32532205527

Repository: https://github.com/shaikidris/FirstPassageLinearTransport-Palomar
Commit: 1b928803af7bc1b5b9278b7328f5497786765371

The manifest pins ProofWidgets commit be3b2e63b1bbf496c478cef98b86972a37c1417d, which is correctly tagged and published upstream as v0.0.87. It appears Palomar’s commit-only dependency checkout does not contain that tag, so Mathlib’s cache command fails while validating proofwidgets:release with “no release tag found.”

The report says not to change the repository and classifies the problem as Palomar-owned. Should I wait for a verifier fix and resubmit the same commit?

There is also a minor diagnostic inconsistency: retryable: false accompanies an instruction to retry later.

mechanical-report-s534pqdw0rq5.zip
Attaching the report for quick reference.
The ProofWidgets problem is now fixed! @Idris Ali Shaik

Thank you!
I retried the unchanged commit after PR #107 using submission bw86tp7fylhf:
https://github.com/PalomarRegistry/PalomarSubmission/actions/runs/32624258792

The tag fix works: Lake now resolves ProofWidgets release v0.0.87.

The trusted-cache stage instead fails with curl: (23) Failure writing output to destination for .lake/packages/proofwidgets/.lake/ProofWidgets4.tar.gz. This appears to be the sandbox write allowlist: the cache phase permits the package’s .lake/build and .lake/config, but the release facet writes the archive directly under .lake. No repository change appears necessary. 

curl: (23) Failure writing output to destination

error: external command 'curl' exited with code 23

✖ [2/2] Running proofwidgets:release

error: failed to fetch GitHub release (see 'proofwidgets:optRelease' for details)

Some required targets logged failures:
* proofwidgets:release


lake stderr:

error: build failed

uncaught exception: Failed to fetch ProofWidgets cloud release: lake failed with error code 1

Error: Process completed with exit code 1. here

Could Palomar allow that exact verifier-controlled archive path, or fetch it before entering the restricted cache run? @Kim Morrison
